discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single solid-state spins (nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond), establishing room-temperature quantum sensing
subfield: Quantum physics / solid-state spin qubits and quantum sensing
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko were the first to optically detect magnetic resonance of a single defect spin in a solid. They then demonstrated coherent control and long-lived quantum coherence of individual nitrogen-vacancy spins and their coupling to nearby nuclear spins, all at room temperature. Lukin showed that these isolated quantum systems could serve as nanoscale magnetometers, and with Wrachtrup and others he realized sensing of single electron and nuclear spins, nanoscale NMR, and quantum registers built from proximal nuclei. Together this work turned a fragile quantum property into a robust, engineerable measurement tool. It created a field: quantum sensing with solid-state spins, now used in condensed-matter physics, biology and geoscience. It also seeded spin-photon quantum networks and inspired a family of new defect qubits in silicon carbide and other hosts. This is a decisive physics achievement with wide and lasting impact.
